I am a woman farming here in Lindi, and life is not easy. The rains can be tricky but we depend on them — I have no pump, no pipes, only the sky. Chemical fertilizer is too costly for me and the shops are far, so I rely on the manure from my few goats and chickens, and I plant my maize together with pigeon peas and cowpeas to keep the soil strong. I save my own seeds from last year like my mother taught me, and my children and I do most of the work ourselves; only at weeding and harvest do I call one or two neighbors to help.
